newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAFRICA BOARD TO PAY FINAL MAIZE POOL PROCEEDS.
newsitem.headline: SAFRICA BOARD TO PAY FINAL MAIZE POOL PROCEEDS.

text.p: South Africa's Maize Board will pay a final 85.04 million rand from its export pools to deliverers from last season, the board said on Thursday.
The Board, which ceased all intervention in the country's maize market from the start of the season on May 1 this year, said the payment would be the last that producers would receive.
Maize Board Chairman Vic Mouton said with the payment, the total price of maize delivered to the board's export pools for the season were:
- For white maize to the board's first pool 604.32 rand a tonne, 592.31 rand for pool two and 566.68 rand for pool three
- For yellow maize 698.65 rand a tonne for pool one, 690.97 rand for pool two and 582.36 rand for pool three.
"This is the last payment that producers will receive from the board and our best wishes go with maize farmers in their new marketing process," Mouton said.
All South Africa's commodity control boards are required to wind down their activities following the passing of the Marketing of Agricultural Products Act last year.
